cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 45 on-track passes, 42 pit stops, 6 cars that never finished, 2 virtual safety cars and a red flag that stopped the race.

cards.title: 19 places changed hands on track before the first lap was done
cards.text: 22 cars into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks.
bullets: 4 drivers gained 2 places each, the most of anybody
cards.note: Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the race.

cards.title: 9 incidents looked at
cards.text: Every one of them logged by race control during the race.
bullets: Lap 1: Lindblad, yellow flag infringement
5 ended in a penalty, 2 in no further action and 2 left for after the race

cards.title: Verstappen is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 1 of 72, in a Red Bull.
bullets: Started P7
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: The race was stopped
cards.text: Red flag: everybody into the pit lane and a wait for the track to be made safe.
bullets: Norris was leading when it happened
Standing restart on lap 3
cards.note: Teams can change tyres while the cars wait, which rewrites the strategies on the grid.

cards.title: Alonso starts P18. Where does he finish?
cards.text: 72 laps to make up ground from there.

cards.title: Bearman is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 3 of 72, in a Haas.
bullets: P16 at the start of lap 2
Started P20
Race control logged an incident with Bearman on lap 3

cards.title: 8 passes on this lap alone
cards.text: Only moves made on track count here, at racing speed.
bullets: 6 different drivers gained a place on this lap
cards.note: A couple of laps after the restart, with the field still sorting itself out.

cards.title: Antonelli takes the lead from Norris
cards.text: A pass for the lead, made on track at racing speed.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 5 times
cards.text: Race control waves a yellow for anything on or near the track that should not be there.
bullets: A yellow means slow down and do not overtake in that part of the track

cards.title: 5 penalties handed out
cards.text: Given by the stewards during the race.
bullets: Lindblad: a drive-through for yellow flag infringement
Colapinto: a drive-through for yellow flag infringement
Colapinto: a 10s penalty for yellow flag infringement
And 2 more
cards.note: A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left. A drive-through is a trip down the pit lane at the speed limit without stopping.

cards.title: 12 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track, and the lap simply stops counting if you leave it.
bullets: Hulkenberg, Sainz and Albon lost 2 each, the most of anybody
cards.note: Keep doing it and it turns into a penalty.

cards.title: Track at 31°C at the start, rising to 33°C at the flag
cards.text: Track temperature changes how much grip the tyres find and how fast they wear. Rain was recorded during the race.

cards.title: Ocon: 6 passes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in a Haas.
bullets: P15 on the grid, and did not reach the flag
cards.note: Only moves made on track count, with the car ahead at racing speed.

cards.title: Lindblad hit 336 km/h
cards.text: The fastest car in a straight line is often not the fastest car over a lap.
bullets: Lindblad did it in a Racing Bulls car
cards.note: Top speed says as much about wing level, and about sitting in somebody's tow, as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It usually lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it.
cards.reveal: Leclerc on lap 60, 1:14.230, in a Ferrari.

cards.kicker: Your call on the pit wall
cards.title: You are Norris, 1.1s behind Antonelli and going nowhere. Now what?
cards.text: Stuck behind another car your tyres overheat and the car will not turn. Stopping first gives you clean track for two or three laps, which is the whole trick behind the undercut.

choices.label: Box now and undercut
choices.sub: Fresh tyres, clean air, two laps to make it pay

choices.label: Stay out and overcut
choices.sub: Let him stop first, then push on an empty track

choices.label: Forget strategy, pass him
choices.sub: Send it and take the risk

outcomes.box: You spend about 18s in the lane and come out in traffic, betting that two fast laps on new tyres are worth more than the place you just gave up.
outcomes.wait: You stay on old rubber while he gets new ones, and you need clean air plus a mistake from him to make it work.
outcomes.attack: Passing a car with the same tyres on the same fuel is the hardest thing in the sport, and running into the back of him ends both races.

cards.reveal: Norris came in on lap 47, 13 laps after this. He finished P1, Antonelli P2.

cards.title: Gasly: 9 laps within a second of the car ahead
cards.text: The longest unbroken run like it in the race, from lap 27 to lap 35, at racing speed.
bullets: 8 other drivers had a run of five laps or more like it
cards.note: Following closely costs the car downforce and cooks the front tyres, so sitting there is harder than it looks.

cards.title: 42 stops, and the busiest lap saw 5 of them
cards.text: Once one car stops, the cars around it have to answer.
bullets: Busiest single lap was 21, with 5 cars in
Shortest time in the pit lane: Hulkenberg, 17.0s
Longest: Piastri, 20.2s
cards.note: Pit lane time runs from the entry line to the exit line, stop included.

cards.title: Lap 35: an incident between Piastri and Hamilton at Turn 1. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and it lands on your desk. Same call the stewards had to make.

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the race on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if there is no stop left. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards took no further action.

cards.title: 111 blue flags waved
cards.text: That is how often a lapped car was told to let the leaders through.

cards.title: Stroll is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 46 of 72, in an Aston Martin.
bullets: P18 at the start of lap 45
Started P19
3 on-track passes before it happened
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Antonelli had the quickest median racing lap
cards.text: No lap 1, no laps in or out of the pits, nothing behind the safety car or the VSC, and the slow outliers trimmed. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Ocon is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 53 of 72, in a Haas.
bullets: P14 at the start of lap 52
Started P15
6 on-track passes before it happened
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Everybody slows down, nobody bunches up
cards.text: Every car is held to a delta time exactly where it is. The gaps freeze instead of vanishing, which is the whole difference from a real safety car.
bullets: Norris was leading when it was called
Bortoleto, Hamilton, Leclerc and 2 others stopped under it
Lifted on lap 57
cards.note: A stop under a VSC costs less than one at racing speed, because everybody else is going slowly too. Cheaper, not free: the leader keeps his gap and the queue behind him keeps its shape.

cards.title: Leclerc: 1:14.230
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all race, in a Ferrari.
bullets: Set on lap 60 of 72, late on, where they usually land
By then the fuel is nearly gone and the car is at its lightest
It is worth no points: the bonus point for it was dropped after 2024

cards.title: Bottas is out

bullets: P18 at the start of lap 61
Started P21
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: One of these three does not see the chequered flag. Who?
cards.text: Nothing on the timing screens says it is coming.
cards.reveal: Albon, on lap 67 of 72. The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Bortoleto went the other way: 4 places lost
cards.text: Qualifying promised one thing and the race delivered another.
bullets: P9 on the grid, P13 at the flag
3 stops when most of the field made 2
Qualifying rewards whoever can put one lap together. A race asks for 72 of them

cards.title: Albon is out
cards.text: His race ends on lap 67 of 72, in a Williams.
bullets: P15 at the start of lap 66
Started P16
1 on-track pass before it happened
cards.note: The timing feed records that he stopped, not why.

cards.title: Albon was P15 a lap before his race ended on lap 67. Where does he finish if it had not?
cards.text: Nobody can answer this one for certain. You have his own lap times to go on and nothing else.

choices.label: He stays about where he was

cards.reveal: Our read from his own lap times, not a fact. He was lapping 2.78s a lap slower than Norris, who went on to win it. With 5 laps left, "he stays about where he was" is the honest guess, and nobody gets to check.

cards.title: Alonso: P18 on the grid, P9 at the flag
cards.text: 9 places gained.
bullets: 2 on-track passes along the way
3 cars that started ahead of him retired

cards.title: Everybody slows down, nobody bunches up
cards.text: Every car is held to a delta time exactly where it is. The gaps freeze instead of vanishing, which is the whole difference from a real safety car.
bullets: Norris was leading when it was called
Lifted on lap 70
cards.note: A stop under a VSC costs less than one at racing speed, because everybody else is going slowly too. Cheaper, not free: the leader keeps his gap and the queue behind him keeps its shape.

cards.title: Alonso ran one set for 37 laps
cards.text: The longest anybody stayed out on one set.
bullets: On the hards, lap 35 to lap 71
cards.note: Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane. And every lap you stretch is a set of tyres getting slower underneath you.

cards.title: Norris wins it
cards.text: P1 Norris · P2 Antonelli · P3 Russell.
bullets: After 72 laps, Antonelli crossed the line 11.536s behind

cards.title: How far behind was Antonelli at the flag?
cards.text: 72 laps, 1 hour 37 minutes of racing, and it comes down to this one number.
cards.reveal: 11.536 seconds after 72 laps. A trip down the pit lane took about 18s today, which is 1.6 times the margin this race was decided by.
